architecture.approach: Add one private workspace package, packages/shared (@riaya/shared), that holds a zod schema per shared contract and infers each type from it, exported from a single entry point. Consumers resolve TypeScript source through the workspace link (no build step). pnpm-workspace.yaml gains packages/*; server and backoffice add the dependency; the two back-office pages that locally duplicate a login/change-password shape move to the shared schema while keeping their own i18n messages. The API keeps validating through class-validator and its ValidationPipe.

dataModel.flowDescription: No database change. A consumer imports a schema and its inferred type from @riaya/shared, validates the input it owns with schema.parse, and uses the type for payloads it sends or receives. No endpoint, Prisma model or stored data is affected.

securityConsiderations.description: The package declares only zod, so server gains no UI dependency; its dependency graph is inspected after the install.
No import may reach outside packages/shared/src, and no env or network access is allowed; verified by reading the whole package tree.
CON-519: the package reads no environment variable and contains no credential; the schemas describe password rules, never values.
CON-515: the API keeps validating through class-validator and the ValidationPipe; the shared schema is not substituted into any guard, pipe or interceptor in this version.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: No build step and no dist: consumers resolve TypeScript source through the workspace link, so there is no artefact to keep in sync or rebuild.

risks.description: The package points main/types at TypeScript source and a consumer's tooling refuses it.
risks.mitigation: Phase 1 finishes with a workspace install plus a typecheck of both consumers importing a trivial export, before any schema exists.

risks.description: The shared schema and a class-validator DTO disagree after an API change.
risks.mitigation: FR-007 makes the comparison explicit; AC-007/AC-008 are the checks and the DTO stays the API's source of truth.

risks.description: Removing the local login schema breaks a page's message handling.
risks.mitigation: EC-003: the page keeps its own i18n messages; only the structure moves, and the page is typechecked after the swap.

risks.description: The package becomes a home for client code or UI strings.
risks.mitigation: FR-006/NFR-003 constrain it, the component list states exactly what may exist, and AC-005 inspects the tree.

risks.description: A second zod major enters the workspace through the new dependency.
risks.mitigation: FR-004/EC-004 require the override's range; the installed tree is inspected for a single resolved zod version.
